Checked against the code: container StartBuild (holder netns, relay via startSessionAndRelay, req.Timeout context, deferred teardown) and Exec (startEnvironment(true) hold mode, waitHeld, ContainerExec shell, teardown on return); qemu New/StartBuild (Accel/QEMUBinary empty means detectAccel/qemuBinary auto-detect; relay VM plus build VM on a socket vlan); vz New (defaultCacheDir) and StartBuild (host relay process, socketpair); winguest BuildGuestCIDR (10.0.0.2/30, the other host of 10.0.0.1's /30); ErrExecNotSupported (qemu, vz, hyperv/driver_windows.go:230). None is boilerplate that misdescribes behavior, apart from the vz platform wording in finding 3. Each Close comment is accurate because every build defers its own teardown.

The second %w is correct. Go 1.20+ fmt.Errorf wraps several errors, and errors.Is/As walk both. lastErr is always non-nil at the return (it is set before the select). The message text is unchanged, because %w formats like %v. No caller branches on the chain in a way the change affects (driver/session.go only checks *url.Error elsewhere). The new test proves it: the mutation run fails both subtests. One theoretical flake: if the deadline lands during an in-flight attempt, lastErr is a context error and errors.As(*net.OpError) fails. A dial to a closed loopback port is refused in microseconds, so the window is negligible (10/10 green).

The nolint is narrow and sound. It covers one line and names one linter, forbidigo, which tier 1's golangci config enables for '^panic$'. The root .golangci.yml does not enable forbidigo or nolintlint, so the directive is inert there and harmless. The reason is accurate: since Go 1.24, crypto/rand.Reader never returns an error and crashes the program on an entropy-source failure, and go.mod is go 1.26.3. With a positive big.Int bound, the err branch is effectively unreachable. The three-line comment above the panic restates the trailer's reason, but it is the 'why' GLOBAL-01 allows.
